properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-04-27 to Chief Oil & Gas Llc in Overton Twp, Bradford county. 78a81(a)3 - CASING AND CEMENTING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to prevent pollution or diminution of fresh groundwater.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Chief Oil & Gas Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-04-27
Violation Code: 78a81(a)3 - CASING AND CEMENTING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to prevent pollution or diminution of fresh groundwater.
Violation ID: 883513
Permit API: 015-23428
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Overton Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2020-04-27
Comments: In an effort to prevent the spread of the COVID-19 virus, the Department has conducted this administrative inspection in response to information provided by Chief. Based on the analytical results for isotopic samples collected by Chief at the above-referenced well on 6/17/2019 and 11/15/2019, methane was detected as follows: 48.53 % Methane detected at the Intermediate (9 5/8¿) x Surface (13 3/8¿) casing annulus on 6/17/2019. 4.16 % Methane detected at the Surface casing (13 3/8¿) x Conductor (20¿) annulus on 11/15/2019. 90.35 % Methane detected at the Intermediate (9 5/8¿) x Surface (13 3/8¿) casing annulus on 11/15/2019. 90.52 % Methane detected at the Production (5 ½") x Intermediate (9 5/8¿) casing annulus on 11/15/2019. The presence of methane at the Surface casing (13 3/8¿) x Conductor (20¿) is evidence of defective cement with methane outside of the surface casing string. As a result, violations of 25 Pa. Code §78a.73(b), §78a81(a)(2) and (3), and §78a.85(a)(5) have been cited. Please note that because your company provided a self-reported notification, no violation was cited for 25 Pa. Code §78a.86, defective cement, for the other annuli where methane was detected. However, Chief is required to comply with the Department¿s regulations, 25 Pa. Code §78a.86, which provides: ¿In a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing, the operator shall report the defect to the Department within 24 hours of discovery by the operator and shall correct the defect. The operator shall correct the defect or submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. If the defect cannot be corrected or an alternate method is not approved by the Department, the well shall be plugged under § 78a.91 ¿ 78a.98 (related to plugging).¿ Therefore, please provide a written response within 30 days of receipt of this Notice of Violation, as to when and how the above listed violations were or will be corrected, and what steps are being taken to prevent their recurrence.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-05-27 to Leatherwood Llc in Franklin Twp, Greene county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Leatherwood Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-05-27
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 885731
Permit API: 059-23032
Unconventional: No
County: Greene
Municipality: Franklin Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-05-27
Comments: On 5/27/2020 at approximately 1030, a follow-up inspection was conducted in response to violations issued on 4/12/2019 (Inspection 2882118). I was accompanied by PA DEP James Kulha. Per the 12/10/2019 letter, the Department has approved the Final Report/remedial Action Completion Report" submitted for the Alternative Remediation of this site. Conductivity was measured in various locations around the well and brine tank and do not appear to be significantly elevated. Vegetation growth adjacent to the brine tank remains distressed (Photo# 9). The Department recommends adding additional seed/mulch to the area. A discarded oil drum was observed on the site next to a brine tank that does not appear to be in use. The drum is labeled "Conklin oil + sand" and appears to be leaking. A petroleum odor was observed in the area (Photos#3-6). The Department recommends that this waste drum and affected soil be removed to prevent further contamination. A slope failure was observed adjacent to the well site (Photo# 7). The Department recommends that this slope failure be temporarily stabilized and remediated in order to achieve site stabilization. A leak was observed on the concrete below the pump jack (Photo# 10). The Department recommends that the well equipment be inspected and the leaked substance be cleaned up to prevent further contamination at the site. Violations are recurring at the site with regards to fluid disposal. Additionally, violations are being issued in regards to the observed slope failure.

Permit API: 083-46720
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/07/2026
Comments: I conducted a follow up inspection of this conventional well that had a release occur in November of 2025, when a steel gathering line had ruptured resulting in crude oil contaminating ditches and soil. Initially the remediation of the site was progressing. There had been no signs of product at the under flow dams, there was no viable oil in the ditches. In preperation of obtaining confirmatory soil samples to evaluate if the remediation was sufficient, it was discovered another leak had developed on a different section of the same line. This operator indicated they will replace all of the steel line for this well with plastic/poly line. This release was caught early and as of now, appears to be less than 1 bbl of lost product and has impacted a minimal amount of soil.Bull Run employees had a roll off dumpster en-route to remove the impacted soil. The ruptured line was sucked out with a vac truck and will be removed while running new poly line. Further inspections will be conducted to document ongoing remedation efforts, as well as confirmatory sampling to show that the remediation is sufficient.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/05/2025 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Susquehanna Township, Cambria county. 78.66(b) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to report a reportable release of brine on or into the ground at the well site within 2 hours after detecting or discovering the releases.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/05/2025
Violation Code: 78.66(b) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to report a reportable release of brine on or into the ground at the well site within 2 hours after detecting or discovering the releases.
Violation ID: 8232577
Permit API: 021-21034
Unconventional: No
County: Cambria
Municipality: Susquehanna Township
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 5/05/2025
Comments: This is an Admin inspection documenting the reporting of a spill that was discovered onsite reportedly by the operator at 1:00 PM on 5/05/2025. According to the Spill Report (attached) that was received the same day at 2:53 PM from Diversified representative Will Warfel, an estimated 30 barrels of brine water was released from the brine tank. According to the spill report, no water resources were affected. No cleanup crews were currently onsite at the time of reporting.The Department contacted Mr. Warfel via phone upon receiving this spill report. During this phone conversation, Warfel further explained an earthen berm surrounds the brine tank, which contained the majority of the released brine. A small amount of brine reportedly escaped and rolled about 30 feet downslope. Mr. Warfel stated that a stream/tributary is audible from the location of the release, however he reported that the released brine does not pose the potential to threaten this water resource as its location is not close enough to be visible from the brine release location. Mr. Warfel then confirmed that 30 barrels of brine was released based on the most recent tank reading, and estimated that 5 barrels of brine was released outside of the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank. Excavation equipment are to be transported onsite for removal of impacted material. The Department recommended during this phone conversation that any remaining impacted material is covered with a waterproof material if rain is forecasted prior to starting remediation.Photos were provided via email by Mr. Warfell. They are attached to this report. Upon review, the time-stamps on the attached photos appear to be 12:30 PM and 12:31 PM, which is prior to when the spill was reported to be discovered, and greater than two hours prior to receipt of the attached spill report. Because the operator failed to report this spill within two hours of detection, a violation shall be noted and immediately corrected.A follow-up site inspection is scheduled to be conducted by the Department in response to this spill notification on 5/06/2025. Violations may be forthcoming pending site inspection and review by the Department.

Report Details

Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 926186
Permit API: 129-26518
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2021
Comments: On August 4, 2021, I conducted an inspection of the Lamacz #1 well site in Penn Township, Westmoreland County. The inspection was conducted as follow up to a release reported to the Department on 7/19/2021, see inspection #3222750 for previous observations and violations related to the release. At the time of inspection, the impacted material appeared to be excavated and placed under a plastic tarp on the well site. The impacted excavation area appeared to be 30’x60’ and approximately 10’ in depth. The excavation appeared to be following a buried black plastic pipe possibly the gathering pipeline. The excavation of the flow path appeared to be 6" deep, 10’ wide and 500’ in length. The excavation appears to be similar to the impacted location observed on 7/19/2021. The operator has installed temporary ES BMPs and what appear to be oil booms on the excavated flow path. The remediation of spill on the well site has uncovered and damaged what appears to be an encapsulated drill pit or onsite waste disposal location. I observed three sections of the torn black plastic sheeting at different elevation within the excavation. The material contained between the black plastic sheets appeared to be dark gray in color and approximately 2" thick. I recommend that the operator identify the contents of the dark gray material and remediate as needed based on the common constituents/indicators of a release related to brine and cuttings. Violations remain outstanding as they relate to the release on 7/19/2021. Additional violations maybe pending further investigation.

Comments: On 09/24/2024 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow up inspection of Chesapeake Appalachia's Hillis Location Well Pad in Herrick Township, Bradford County. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days.

Permit API: 031-23676
Unconventional: No
County: Clarion
Municipality: Monroe Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/26/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow up to Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection inspection #4020256 conducted on July 24, 2025 at 0907 hrs. During the inspection, the wellhead and casing strings were visually assessed for signs of leakage, structural deterioration, and or failure. While on-site the well was shut in and not producing. The 7" intermediate casing was being vented to atmosphere through the annulus vent valve at a concentration of 97% combustible gas. The landowner is no longer receiving gas from this well. To evaluate the potential for subsurface gas migration, four slam bar holes were installed approximately 6 inches to 1 foot from the well-bore in the cardinal directions. Each hole was placed to a depth of approximately 3 feet. Soil gas measurements were obtained using a Bascom-Turner Gas Explorer II meter, calibrated on March 26, 2026. All slam bar holes at the time of inspection were non-detect for combustible gas. As of the completion of this inspection, the operator has not plugged the well nor remedied any of the outstanding violations associated with the well. A previous check valve violation created in error has been closed.

Comments: An oil release to ground from a malfunctioning valve on the discharge pipe of one of the two tanks located in secondary containment at this well site was reported by Kenneth Fleeman on April 11, 2019. Oil was released from the tank by a malfunctioning valve which resulted in oil flow to the southwest end of the secondary containment where it disappeared into the stony soil. There is dead vegetation and oily pools of water observed to the east, south and west of the secondary containment. A 200 foot path of dead vegetation extends south of the well site. The path of dead vegetation disappears on the slope south of the well site and does not appear to have reached any waterways. A patch of dead vegetation and several oily pools of water is evident 15' east of the secondary containment. There is a 50' to 70' path of vegetation to the southwest however the oil does not appear to have moved any farther. Abarta Production Supervisor, Scott Patterson, stated that all tanks and piping were intact at the time of his inspection of the well on April 1, 2019 and the tank had approximately 13" of oil (10.75 barrels) at that time. All oil above the the discharge pipe was released to ground. Based on conductivity testing this was an oil release only, no brine was released. This is a violation of PA Oil and Gas Regulations and a clean-up process will be required. You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil &Gas Well Sites or Access Road. This Policy sets forth the procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow up to Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection inspection #4020256 conducted on July 24, 2025 at 0907 hrs. During the inspection, the wellhead and casing strings were visually assessed for signs of leakage, structural deterioration, and or failure. While on-site the well was shut in and not producing. The 7" intermediate casing was being vented to atmosphere through the annulus vent valve at a concentration of 97% combustible gas. The landowner is no longer receiving gas from this well. As of the completion of this inspection, the operator has not plugged the well nor remedied any of the outstanding violations associated with the well. A previous check valve violation created in error has been closed.

Comments: On January 13 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Aphrodite Well Site (ESCGP issued on 5/9/2020, amended on 2/5/2024, expiring on 2/4/2029) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 1/12/2026 (CTS 394575). Present during the inspection was operator representative Justin Miller.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel.At the time of inspection, there are 5 total wells on the well pad. According to the operator, stimulation for all 5 wells has been completed and they are preparing to conduct drill outs and flowback operations over the next 3 weeks.Upon inspection, it appeared the stimulation equipment was being demobilized. The drilling equipment still onsite appeared to be within secondary containment. The secondary containment appeared to be installed correctly with no tears or leaks. During the inspection, Mr. Miller guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Miller the release occurred on 1/13/2026. He stated the release occurred from a loose hose connection from one of the tanks. At the time of the inspection the operator is estimating a total release of 15 gallons of a produced water was released to the graveled well pad.The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the spill was in an approximate 4 foot by 20 foot area outside of the secondary containment for the tanks next to a GPU. Conductivity readings including several readings of OR (Over Detectable Range, >20MS) , 11.46mS, and 1.57mS, were obtained in the area of the release. During the inspection, the Department observed 2 small areas of excavation. Mr. Miller stated that additional excavation will occur as needed when the containment is removed from its location.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued against the Aphodite 2M well for the observed release.

Violation ID: 8242707
Permit API: 129-29266
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/29/2025
Comments: On July 29, 2025, the DEP conducted an Incident Inspection of EQTs Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 7/28/2025 at 2:54 pm.The spill report stated that at 2:06 pm on 7/28/2025, over 5 gallons of production fluids were found on the gravel well pad at the Porter Well site after removing secondary containment. Accompanying during today's inspection is EQTs representative Kyle Borden.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed an Act 9 Sign posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the on-site mailbox, the DEP observed both an Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan, that had different Operator information on it than the Act 9 sign. The DEP recommends the Operator update the plans as applicable. At the time of this inspection, drill outs were recently completed on the 6U and containment was removed from the well pad the day prior. Mr. Borden stated that the secondary containment in the release area was packed with tanks and large equipment, therefore despite routine inspections of the containment, only the edges of the containment could be inspected, and no holes or tears were observed. However, upon removal of the containment, staining and small puddles were observed on the gravel pad in an approximately 115 ft x 60 ft area. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the area of the graveled pad where this incident occurred to be adjacent to wellheads covered by boxes. The pea gravel in this area was observed to be wet with sections that appeared to be darker in color than other areas. Mr. Borden stated that SPSI and Moody were arriving on site to remediate the release and that they estimate remediation to be completed within the day. EQT representative Schuyler Brounce mentioned in his email (documented in IR 4024285), that following his review of the incident, he estimates the release to be over 1 barrel. At the time of this inspection, Mr. Borden stated once all contaminated gravel has been removed, an updated quantity will be provided to the DEP.At the time of this inspection, the DEP utilized a conductivity meter to screen the graveled well pad. The DEP collected soil readings of 1.835 mS, 3.22 mS, 3.35 mS and 2.08 mS in the incident area closest to the wellheads, as well as 2.56 mS between two wellheads and a fluid reading of Over Range in fluid observed to be pooled in secondary containment adjacent to the release area. These conductivity readings are elevated when compared to the background soil reading of 0.1457 mS collected in vegetation by the Act 9 Sign.At the time of this inspection, the DEP requested secondary containment logs for the Porter well pad and Mr. Borden stated they would be provided to the Department electronically. The DEP is also requesting an electronic copy of the Safety Data Sheets for all chemicals stored/utilized within and near the secondary containment that was observed to have the release underneath by COB 8/5/2025.The DEP recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(2).Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the over 1 barrel release of production fluids on the graveled well pad.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations and how the Operator quantified the amount released. The Operator will need to follow Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) and assess the impacts to the Water of the Commonwealth from the release.

Comments: On December 3, 2025, the Department conducted a follow-up inspection to IR 4095466 at the former location of the MAWC well site in Springfield Township, Fayette County. A violation was issued in IR 4095466 for failure to restore the well site by 10/30/2025, in accordance with the 5/01/2025 amendment of the 12/16/2021 CO and A. The Department requested an NOV Response to IR 4095466 from the operator by December 4, 2025.The First Modification to the COA was entered on 5/01/2025. Paragraph 3i of the 12/16/2021 CO and A states: "M4 shall immediately commence work to completely restore the Well sites upon execution of the First Amendment and complete restoration of the Well Sites by October 30, 2025, in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas act, 58 Pa.C.S. 3216, the site restoration regulations set forth in 25 Pa. Code 78a.65, and all applicable provisions of the Clean Streams Law and the regulations promulgated thereunder. M4 shall submit form 8000 PM-OOGN0075, "Well Site Restoration Report," within sixty (60) days of restoring the Well Sites." Site restoration is to be conducted "as closely to original conditions as practicable, including restoration of original contours and capability of supporting land uses existing prior to drilling of the Well(s) by October 30, 2025, unless M4 obtains a signed and notarized written consent of the landowner to leave the Well Site in an altered state".The following was observed:The Act 9 sign remains installed at the entrance of the access road (photo 1). No restoration plans were found on site during this inspection. Although site stabilization and progress of restoration could not be completely evaluated during this inspection due to the snow cover, it is still evident through the snow cover that the site has not attained greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth (photos 5, 8, and 9). The Department recommends that the operator assess the site for temporary stabilization upon dissipation of the snow cover, and apply additional mulch and seed if needed.Based on observations from this inspection, the violation issued in IR 4095466 shall remain outstanding.

Comments: This conventional well is equipped with rods and tubing. The pump jack has been removed from the well, the annulus of the well remains connected to a gathering line. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. The well is not equipped with a well tag, nor is there a site ID sign posted at the location.A tank battery containing four steel tanks and two poly tanks inside of an earthen containment is located approximately 200 feet east of this well. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/15/2022 to PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC in Hamilton Twp, McKean county. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/15/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 948069
Permit API: 083-49666
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/15/2022
Comments: This inspection was performed following a report of an oil and gas leak in the vicinity of Chappel Fork near the road crossing of RT 321 (CTS #362745). At the time of the report to DEP, I spoke to the complainant and determined the location to begin searching. I contacted Pennhills Resources as they have wells in the immediate vicinity, and we agreed to meet on site to look. After beginning at Rt 321 we headed east until we found some oil collected in a low spot. It appears as though a line has burst with some gas pressure on the line, causing oil and gas to bubble to the surface. The oil then flowed south and into a low swale, where the majority of it collected. Some crude then flowed through into a channel formed by the collection of two spring runs, and toward the main branch of Chappel Fork. Oil was collecting behind ice pockets and in between leaves and dead vegetation for approximately 200 feet. A small amount of sheen was noted in Chappel Fork, but no free product. Approximately 15-20 barrels of oil was emitted from the line in total. Another small area nearer to the creek when following the line was noted to contain some basic sediment and paraffin at the surface and under a hemlock tree; it is uncertain if this is another leak site or simply product following the line. Pennhills immediately moved to contain the spill with booms in the back channel, and then brought a mini excavator to site to dig up the line and slow the leak. The 2" line was uncovered and a band placed on the line, which was broken on the bottom. It was determined that the old access past well 9A could be used to mobilize equipment and some brush was removed to make for better access. A vac truck was brought to site to collect any free product available, which was able to get a large amount on the first load. It was determined the evening of 3/15 that the line belonged to Pennhills, who will be continuing to clean up the oil and soil until clean. The operator built two underflow dams to contain any free product flowing down the channel with melting ice starting to give way. Followup inspection will be performed as necessary.

Comments: On 6/2/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 60 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. When I arrived at the active north pad, I met with Seneca's Mark McCormick who described current operations as follows: Evolution Well Services has been on site since 2/13/2026, performing stimulation operations on eight recently drilled gas wells. The crew was currently alternating between the 70HU, 204HU, 203HU, and had just finished the 72HU on 6/1/2026. The crew has completed the stages on the other four wells. Mark expects stimulation activities on the eight wells to be completed by 6/9/2026.Stimulation operations were being conducted within secondary containment. There were 32 frac tanks stationed in secondary containment on the west side of the pad, four for freshwater and 28 for produced water. Additionally, there were four pump down frac tanks, two gas buster frac tanks and five working frac tanks staged in secondary containment on the pad. Chemical tanks and totes were staged in secondary containment.Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs that are connected to the completed wells were stationed in secondary containment.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. The original south pad and access road for the Taft 851 1V well have been returned to original grade, the well pad and associated diversion berms were adequately stabilized. Separate construction projects are underway, installing water and gas pipelines on the south side of the pad.During the inspection, I field screened the following for conductivity: A 2' x 3' puddle of water above the center outfall from the north side of the pad, tested at 7.81 mS conductance. Liquid flowing from the center north outfall into the basin tested at 8.08 mS conductance. Liquid in the basin near the northeast outfall tested at 4.04 mS conductance. I met Seneca's Jeff Passerrello on location during the inspection. He was collecting water samples from the location. I discussed my findings with him.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1200 hours.

Inspection Date: 1/29/2026
Comments: On January 29, 2026, the Department conducted an Incident Inspection at Range Resources Shearer Robert tank pad located in Robinson Township, Washington County following a spill that was reported to the DEP on 1/27/2026. Accompanying during today's inspection was Range Resources representative Nate Smiell.Documented in IR 4131333, according to the spill report and the phone conversation with Mr. Zofchak, at approximately 2:55 AM on January 27, 2026 a water truck was staged on the tank pad when a closed valve on the back of the truck began leaking into a bleeder valve hose, subsequently releasing Produced Water onto the gravel pad in an approximately 20 ft by 100 ft area. Water truck drivers contained the release to the graveledwell pad and began vacuuming up the pooled fluid, SPSI arrived on site on 1/27/2026 and began scraping the gravel tank pad. The release was estimated to be approximately 193 gallons, and no waters of the Commonwealth were reportedly impacted.At the time of this inspection, an Act 9 sign was observed at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it and in the on-site mailbox was an Emergency Response Plan, and a Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan, both of which had all required components.At the time of this inspection, Mr. Smiell showed the Department the approximate location of the incident area and stated that SPSI finished scraping the tank pad and filled 2 roll off dumpsters with contaminated gravel on 1/27/2026. The area which appeared to be approximately 100 ft by 20 ft was observed to be recently scraped. Some spray paint was observed on the gravel to mark the areas where Mr. Smiell reported that samples were collected on 1/28/2026 in accordance with Act 2 requirements. Soil conductivity readings could not be collected due to the ground being frozen, however, the Department did not observe any visible evidence of Produced Water remaining on the graveled tank pad. Range is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, and plan for remediation of the violations. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled.Range will need to follow the Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2).Range will also need to assess the impacts to waters of the Commonwealth from the release.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the 193 gallon release of Produced Water onto the graveled tank pad.

Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow-up after the Department discovered fluid with elevated electrical conductivity (EC) in the northwest stormwater channel. Two workover rigs are in operation on the well pad. I met with company man Marc McCartor upon arriving on location. He informed me that no excavation had taken place yet in the northwest stormwater channel. He said a sump was installed at the west corner at the end of the stormwater channel. He said that a vacuum truck is on site sucking up the fluid from the channel and the sump. The EC of the fluid in the sump near the halfway point of the northwest pad edge was 333 uS/cm. Farther west, the EC of the fluid in the channel near the location of the sample taken in the previous inspection on 5/8/24 was 798 uS/cm. Farther west within the channel, the EC was 2.34 mS/cm. In the sump at the west corner of the pad within the liner, the EC of the fluid was 2.01 mS/cm. Under the liner, the EC of the fluid was 1600 uS/cm.The Department recommends continuing to collect and dispose of the fluid in the northwest stormwater channel and in the sump. I made this recommendation to the company man before leaving the location. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21946 for the elevated electrical conductivity fluid discovered by the Department in the northwest stormwater channel on 5/8/24.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21938 for the reported release of produced fluid to the pad surface on 3/1/24.

Comments: On 02/21/2025 an Incident Response inspection was conducted at the DMC Well Site in response to an operator reported release.On 12/21/2024 Range Resources Representative, Derek Zofchak, reported an approximately 25 to 30-gallon release of reused water off containment at the DMC Well pad located in Donegal Township, Washington County.Range Resources representatives, Derek Zofchak and Denny Furmanek, were on site at the time of inspection. Mr. Furmanek and Mr. Zofchak informed the Department that that the release was discovered today (02/21/2025) at 10:55 am, that the quantity released was approximately 25 to 30 gallons, and that remediation efforts had already begun on the impacted area. The source of release was determined to be damaged secondary containment. The secondary containment had been damaged by a truck tire and the fluids on containment overtopped the containment berm and continued off an adjacent duck pond and onto the pad aggregate. Conductivity probe calibrated on 02/21/2025.The following was observed during the inspection:-The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance. Various co-operations were taking place at the time of inspection and frac equipment was observed on site (Photos 1-2).-The area impacted by the release was observed. The area appeared to measure approximately 150 ft in length by 35 ft in width. Pooled fluid with a sheen was observed throughout the area. The damaged secondary containment was observed. It was made known that a crew was on site to repair the damaged containment. A vac truck was observed on site removing pooled fluids in the impacted area and on containment (Photos 3-5).-Field conductivity screening was conducted immediately in front of a large, gray electrical box. Over Range (greater than 20 ms/cm) field conductivity readings were observed (Photos 6-8).-Field conductivity screening was conducted throughout the impacted area. Elevated field screening values ranged between 7.21 ms/cm and greater than 20 ms/cm. The discharge onto the ground and failure to dispose of fluids, specifically produced fluid, are violations of 78a.54, 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act (SWMA) 301. The potential to have indirectly impacted Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC) is a violation of 91.34(a) (Photos 9-12).-The extent of the impacts was observed where a non-elevated field conductivity screening of 1,432 s/cm was observed (Photos 13-14).-Remediation efforts were in progress at the time of inspection. Operators were observed scraping off impacted aggregates with heavy machinery (Photos 15-17).-A roll-off box arrived on site during the inspection. It was stated that the impacted material would be placed in the roll-off box and that waste manifests would be provided to the Department (Photo 18).Determination:Violations issued.

Comments: On 02/21/2025 an Incident Response inspection was conducted at the DMC Well Site in response to an operator reported release.On 12/21/2024 Range Resources Representative, Derek Zofchak, reported an approximately 25 to 30-gallon release of reused water off containment at the DMC Well pad located in Donegal Township, Washington County.Range Resources representatives, Derek Zofchak and Denny Furmanek, were on site at the time of inspection. Mr. Furmanek and Mr. Zofchak informed the Department that that the release was discovered today (02/21/2025) at 10:55 am, that the quantity released was approximately 25 to 30 gallons, and that remediation efforts had already begun on the impacted area. The source of release was determined to be damaged secondary containment. The secondary containment had been damaged by a truck tire and the fluids on containment overtopped the containment berm and continued off an adjacent duck pond and onto the pad aggregate. Conductivity probe calibrated on 02/21/2025.The following was observed during the inspection:-The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance. Various co-operations were taking place at the time of inspection and frac equipment was observed on site (Photos 1-2).-The area impacted by the release was observed. The area appeared to measure approximately 150 ft in length by 35 ft in width. Pooled fluid with a sheen was observed throughout the area. The damaged secondary containment was observed. It was made known that a crew was on site to repair the damaged containment. A vac truck was observed on site removing pooled fluids in the impacted area and on containment (Photos 3-5).-Field conductivity screening was conducted immediately in front of a large, gray electrical box. Over Range (greater than 20 ms/cm) field conductivity readings were observed (Photos 6-8).-Field conductivity screening was conducted throughout the impacted area. Elevated field screening values ranged between 7.21 ms/cm and greater than 20 ms/cm. The discharge onto the ground and failure to dispose of fluids, specifically produced fluid, are violations of 78a.54, 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act (SWMA) 301. The potential to have indirectly impacted Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC) is a violation of 91.34(a) (Photos 9-12).-The extent of the impacts was observed where a non-elevated field conductivity screening of 1,432 s/cm was observed (Photos 13-14).-Remediation efforts were in progress at the time of inspection. Operators were observed scraping off impacted aggregates with heavy machinery (Photos 15-17).-A roll-off box arrived on site during the inspection. It was stated that the impacted material would be placed in the roll-off box and that waste manifests would be provided to the Department (Photo 18).Determination:Violations issued.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/23/2025
Comments: Arrived on site at 20:00 hrs. on 10/22/25 to relieve OGI Dave Schoonover to continue the Departments continuous oversite of well control operations. This morning at approx. 0830 hrs., while performing stimulation ops. on the Lauer 12H a sudden pressure drop was noted. Fluids and gas were noted exiting the well from the (9x5) annulus wing valve, emanating from a needle valve. Stimulation operations were shut down and Operator contacted Cudd Well Control Services to mobilize to location. Currently Operator is containing release to cellar area and pumping fluid to gas buster storage tank on location. Operator will continue monitoring well pressures and venting (9x5) annulus discharges in a safe contained manner until well control can be restored. At approx. 2100 hrs. Cudd Well Control personnel arrived onsite. Cudd and Coterra personnel are currently evaluating well conditions and developing a plan for well intervention. Since the well is stable and being monitored, the decision was made to continue well control operations at first light. Throughout the day and overnight water cannons were being used to mist the well and pad intermittently to keep methane levels low. Coterra has been and will continue monitoring air quality in vicinity of location on an hourly basis. During a 07:00 conference call with Coterra and Department personnel it was confirmed that once the well is killed, Coterra plans to run diagnostic logging tools down hole to assess wellhead and casing conditions to decide the next steps in well control operations. Coterra will keep the Department informed of any new information as it becomes available. OGI Scotty Brown arrived @ ~ 07:45 and we took a walk around site before he relieved me @ 08:00 for day shift.

Violation ID: 8210196
Permit API: 125-29086
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: West Bethlehem Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/04/2024
Comments: On 12/04/2024, an incident inspection was conducted at the EQT GREGOR well site in West Bethlehem Township, Washington County in response to a spill reported by the operator on 12/03/2024.The operator reported that the water truck was offloading, and pressure backfilled into the truck causing overflow out the top of the truck. Approximately 15 gallons of produced water was spilled onto the well pad off containment. The following was observed during inspection: At the time of the inspection, I observed that SPSI appeared to have finished remediation. Approximately 60 x 60 feet of contaminated area was excavated. I observed multiple wet spots within the remediated area. No elevated conductivity was observed around the remediated/excavated and initial spill area (Photo 1-7).Logan Dominick from EQT stated in an email received on 12/05/2024 regarding spill location and updated description:On 12/3/24, we had a water truck off loading at the Comtec stands on the Gregor pad, supporting the frac. During the offloading process, the pump on the Comtec stand malfunctioned, causing the pump to back feed pressure into the truck and caused fluid to be released from the PRV on the truck. Once Environmental was able to investigate further, it was determined that the quantity was right around 1 bbl. This release is being put through Act 2. All remediation was completed the same day and consultant took confirmatory samples. Photos from Logan Dominick were included within the email, post-remediation and pre-remediation (Photo 8-10).Violations are being issued for: 78a.54, 91.34(a), CSL 301, CSL 307(a),SWMA 301, and 78a.57(a)
